blocks.text: During my travels, I have met people from different places, cultures, religions, and backgrounds. Each photograph in this series captures one of those encounters, a face, a gesture, a moment of life. We often define ourselves and others by the things that make us different: the colour of our skin, the language we speak, the religion we follow, or the place we call home. Yet, beneath all these differences, there is something we share: we are humans. These fifteen photographs are not meant to represent a particular culture or identity. They are simply photos of people, people who laugh, struggle, love, dream, work, and live, just as we all do. Just Humans is a reflection on our shared humanity. A reminder that before we are anything else, we are human beings. And perhaps recognizing what we have in common is where understanding, respect, and harmony begin.
